Royal Elite #1

Deviant King

Rina Kent, Unknown Author

3.89
151,162 ratings13,629 reviews
Rate this book
The villain isn't supposed to be king

I have a simple plan.
Finish Royal Elite School and get into my dream university.

One glance from the school’s king blows my plan up in smoke.
One glance and he suffocates my air.
One glance and he issues his death sentence.

His first words spiral my life into irreparable chaos.
“I will destroy you.”

Everything about Aiden King is black.
Black mind.
Black heart.
Black soul.

I should’ve remained quiet and endured the time I have left.
I didn’t.

I made the irrevocable mistake of provoking the king on his throne.
The devil in his hell.

And now, I’ll pay the price.

Being hated by Aiden King is dangerous.
But being wanted by him is lethal.

Deviant King is book one of Royal Elite Series. This is a dark high school bully romance, mature new adult, and contains dubious situations that some readers might find offensive. Aiden isn’t the normal romance hero. In fact, he’s not a hero at ALL. So please don’t read this if any of that bothers you.

Royal Elite
#1 Deviant King
#2 Steel Princess
#3 Twisted Kingdom

This book is part of a trilogy and is NOT a standalone.
The entire trilogy is available.

About the author

Rina Kent

65 books75.5k followers
Rina Kent is a New York Times, USA Today, and #1 bestselling author of all things dark romance.
Better known for writing unapologetic anti-heroes and villains, Rina weaves tales of characters you shouldn’t fall for but inevitably do. Her stories are laced with a touch of darkness, a splash of angst, and just the right amount of unhealthy intensity.
When she’s not busy plotting mayhem for her ever-expanding Rinaverse, she leads a private life in London, travels, and pampers her cats in true Cat Lady fashion.

June 15, 2020
Trigger Warning: You’ll need to surgically remove your feminist brain to survive this book. I tried. I failed. I regret everything.

To the author, a humble suggestion:
“If your book is just an excuse for steamy romance, then for the love of literature, make it hot. Or at least coherent.”
Sadly, this isn’t steamy. It’s just disturbing. This book doesn’t miss the mark — it catapults itself into a black hole of cringe, cliché, and creepiness.

Let me be clear: I love a well-done dark high school romance. Bring on the angst. Bring on the mind games. But this? This reads like someone googled “how to write a problematic alpha male” and then ignored every single red flag.

“There is a fine line between bully romance and outright sexual assault.”
This book crosses it, dances on it, then gaslights you for noticing.

The plot is as sturdy as wet tissue paper. The writing? Imagine someone whispering “sexy” into a fan for 400 pages. The pacing is glacial, the internal monologues are endless, and the scenes are repeated so often it’s like reading a bad fanfic stuck on loop.

The heroine — or as I’ve come to call her: Elsa/Ellie/Elsie/Frozen/Ice-Cube-in-Heels — is the lone flicker of sense in this literary dumpster fire. And even she had me rolling my eyes by chapter five. Yes, she occasionally uses logic (bravo, truly), but she also spends an absurd amount of time bumping into people and yelling “OW!” Like she’s stuck in a never-ending TikTok skit.

And don’t even get me started on Aiden, the “motherfucking king”. More like the mother of all red flags. His version of romance is textbook possessive, controlling, and grossly manipulative — but hey, it’s okay, because he’s hot, right? No. Not in 2025. Not in any timeline where we’ve read better.

A brutal checklist of pain:

First meet with the energy of a broken elevator ✔

Writing so bland, toast is offended ✔

Scenes so repetitive you’d think your Kindle glitched ✔

Side characters straight out of a Wattpad reject pile ✔

“Chemistry” so forced it needed CPR ✔

Cliffhanger? More like a mercy kill ✔

Plot? What plot? ✔

Final thoughts:
This isn’t romance. It’s a trainwreck trying to look seductive. If you value your time, your brain cells, or your taste in fiction — stay far, far away. Burn it, bin it, or bury it under better books. Just don’t read it.

4.5

Well, Rina Kent just left one hell of an impression on me! This story isn't about your average new adult couple, and their romance isn't normal by any means. Prepare to clutch your pearls if you can't deal with sexual situations that aren't exactly consensual. *In other words, heed the content warning before going into this one!*



Like it's stated in the title, Aiden King is one deviant motherfucker! He has no boundaries whatsoever, and his moral compass is broke as fuck. The things he did to Elsa were cruel, crazy, and 100 percent criminal on several occasions. Despite that, I wound up rooting for him in his quest to make Elsa his. 



It makes no sense for me to feel that way, because she honestly needs a restraining order and a psychiatric evaluation. I do too though apparently, because I kept wanting her to give in to a lot of his demands pretty early on in the book! LOL At the same time, I wanted her to fight him and give him a taste of his own medicine, and she did that, too. I can't actually fault Elsa for any of her decisions, because Aiden has me just as fucked up as she is. 



I couldn't get enough of Elsa and Aiden together! I literally read the entire book from start to finish in one sitting. The steamy scenes between the two of them were intense, twisted, and super hot! Their relationship is complicated from the beginning, and just when you think things are starting to make more sense, BAM! Rina Kent throws you a curve ball that knocks your ass out. 



Aside from the romance, I loved the added mystery of Elsa not remembering her past due to experiencing a traumatic event in her childhood. Bits and pieces sneak through in flashbacks and dreams, and I was trying to piece everything together along with Elsa. I love it when the narrator is as in the dark as you are, and if you do too, then you'll definitely enjoy that aspect of the book. 



Deviant King is the first book in a series, so be prepared for a cliffhanger ending. I got enough answers for me to not feel super frustrated by it, but it still left me reeling. I can't wait for the next installment, Steel Princess! Hopefully, we finally get some of Aiden's POV, because so far, the story has been in Elsa's entirely. 



Side note: The side characters in the book intrigued me enough to want more of their stories. Fingers crossed they get books of their own in the future!


I recommend Deviant King to fans of intense dark bully romance and slightly unhinged alphaholes.

"Being hated by Aiden King is dangerous. But being wanted by him is lethal."

Well, this turned out to be much better than what I expected. In no ways is this a perfect book but it has a very addictive quality to it. I couldn't stop reading it at all.

Elsa is such a likable character to me. I absolutely adored her. Hell, she's a total baddie to me. But I will say, she has a tendency to put others before herself once she decides she cares about you. And fine, very admirable trait. But at some point she has to stop being a pushover. The amount of times I would have made Aiden grovel and crawl on his knees for the shit he pulled is unholy. Listen, I'm not proud of it but given the power she knows she holds over him? Make that man earn you. Don't just set boundaries, make him honor those ffs 😩😩🥲 Though I know there's a whole lot of character growth waiting for Elsa in the next book. Her past and the memory fluctuations is interesting.

Aiden is an interesting character. I liked him better than Levi. There's a very menacing sort of charm about Aiden. You hate him and you hate how much you like him. Because why is this man both so frustratingly arrogant and annoying, but so alluring?? And good Lord, the mouth on this man 🫠🫠 He's absolutely filthy and I love it 😩😩🥵 Not that it makes up for the bullshit he pulled throughout the book but he's just the kind of guy who will win you over.

As for the side characters, I'm liking the dynamic between Kimberly and Xander. I'm liking Xander a lot, though he's subtle as a bull with a sledgehammer with his feelings. Kim however, frustrated me a lot. She needs to grow up and confront things. Her constant running away and crying is exhausting. On the other hand, Silver and Cole? Hello??? Am I sensing something in the taboo?? Cause I like the idea a lot 🤨🍿 Cole is the sort of character that appeals to me a lot and would have me purring. Silver, clearly someone with more layers than I'm anticipating despite the bratty, bitchy vibes.

"Everything about Aiden King is black.
Black mind.
Black heart.
Black soul."

The romance between Aiden and Elsa was instant sparks flying for me. I loved the push and pull. The stupid annoying telenovela games Aiden pulled only for him to gravitate back to Elsa. The spice is hot as hell 🥵🥵 And genuinely don't know how Elsa managed to stay sane in this man's presence. But what I would love to see in the next book is him actually earning her. Sure he notices every little thing about her and takes care of her in his own way but his attitude needs to change. In fact, both their attitudes need to mature up.

I'm super intrigued by the ending. The cliffhanger literally made me scream. But thankfully, I don't have to wait to read the next one 😌😌



~•~•~

Fantabulous!




This was such an awesome bully romance. If you like this genre at all, then this is the book for you. The Hero is a huge jerk and a big bully and completely obsessed with the heroine Elsa Quinn. First he bullies her by turning the whole school against her on her first day, then later he bullies her into almost everything she does. She sees emptiness in his eyes, she knows he has something dark inside him.

I had been waiting for this book. Not long ago I read Noble Savages that included the book Cruel King. I love Bully Romance and Cruel King was one of the best I had read and was a step in a new direction for Rina Kent. I think all her Mafia/assassin series books are incredible. Cruel King was the story of Levi King and it included Levi’s cousin Adrian and this book is Adrian’s story. The way Levi talked about Adrian sounded like Adrian could be a sociopath.

Elsa likes to stay in the background but is not afraid to stand up for herself, and while she is afraid of Aiden, she stands up for herself anyway. Though he seems to always see through her. He says she likes being forced into doing things she thinks she should have issues with, and she isn’t sure if he is right or if she just hates him. Maybe she thinks she should because he made her miserable for a long time.

On her first day at Royal Elite School Elsa meets Kim, a girl who is sneaking around the edge of the crowd of students and she figures that Kim is a girl like her, who just wants to keep her head down and get through high school so she can get into a good college. They become immediate friends. Then she sees Aiden on the field with his friends. She meets his eyes and can’t look away. He then comes up to her and tells her that he will destroy her.



Aiden is the king of the school and after that the majority of the student body treats her like trash. El and Aiden have daily glaring matches but other than that, they have no contact. He doesn’t outright bully her, but he also doesn’t do anything about it and since one word from him to the other students would stop it, she blames him for starting it and letting it go on.

Things change on the first day of their senior year when he starts bullying her face to face. He wants her and she is putty in his hands. There are also a lot of secrets at play. Elsa is being raised by her aunt and uncle since her parents died when she was young. She doesn’t remember anything before she woke up in the hospital and doesn’t want to remember.

Also, there is something going on with her friend Kim and Kim won’t talk about what it is, but it is the reason Kim has been an outcast even though she has known 90% of the students since middle school. Kim even lives right near Aiden and across the street from Aidens best friend Xander.

The biggest mystery is Aiden himself. Why is he so dark? When Elsa calls him sick he doesn’t deny it, he knows he is different than other people. Elsa is curious to know what made him that way. She even wonders if he was abused as a child. I love how it is written, with all the mystery and we as readers don’t know the answers either.

But as I stare up at Aiden’s punishing eyes, my earlier thoughts shrink behind my trembling, defective heart. He scares me. Call it instinct or an intuition, but something terrifying lurks behind that easy-going smile and football star image.
“What did you just do?” His voice is calm and quiet with a slight huskiness.

I hate in some books how when the reader knows what the secrets are and the people who have the secrets don’t tell them to each other, so everything is about huge misunderstandings or just the fact that the main character(s) don’t really know the motivation behind certain things the other one does. This book doesn’t do that. The reader is as in the dark about the secrets as the character(s) who don’t know.

Another thing I like was that this was an erotic romance and boy was it spicy. I give it 5 peppers for hotness 🌶🌶🌶🌶🌶! One thing I sometimes hate about high school romance is that they are too clean and a great number of high school students can be a bit dirty. If they were we wouldn’t have TV shows like Teen Mom or Young and Pregnant.

I voluntarily read and reviewed an advanced copy of this book. All thoughts & opinions are my own.

elsa’s inner monologues were an absolute pain to read, i kid you not. i felt like a ping pong ball, bouncing around in that noggin of hers. the saving grace here though was that she was the lesser of two evils. i just know i’d be diving headfirst off my apartment building into oncoming traffic if i had to inhabit aiden’s mind for a single second 🙂‍↔️. her and astrid are in the same whatsapp group though, no cap. dumb one-dimensional erratic heroines club. all that brain mush about these boys being “devils” and “kings” with their “royal decrees” when they are literally puny lil high schoolers with egos the size of jupiter and nothing actionable to back it up besides daddy’s influence fries me to a crisp every single time 😂😂😂. one positive i have about her though is that she did try to have a backbone in the earlier bits, so it wasn’t complete doormat city…up to a point. jury’s out on some of her other behaviour. when she pulled a sasha rubbing up against aiden while he was sleeping, the sound that left my mouth is between me and god. oh, i was SNORT-LAUGHING. that’s the only way to describe it.

everything in here was so overly dramatic to the point of absurdity 😂. i’m realizing that dark romances set in high school are just begging to flop because it all feels so comical, unserious and forced. this book isn’t dark, either. sure, it has some unhinged antics from the mmc but none of it was really convincingly sinister lol. it all felt like cosplay and lecherous neanderthal nonsense. that psycho persona aiden was donning came across to me like a bad toupé popped on top a shiny head, not even glued down. just sitting there, i could yank it off and expose him for the baldy that he truly is. the meager plot tried (like the end served up a lil something, albeit very predictable) but it still just didn’t feel all that intense. not here, not ever 😂.

i’m not even gonna touch the writing quality. at this point, i’m not going into rina books hoping for miracles on this front — believe me on that. did she punctuate several sentences with the word “dickhead”? sure. i’ll allow. unfortunately, this rating is really about me simply not “vibing” with the couple or the “plot” in any sort of un-ironic way. why do i keep coming back, you may ask? i just want another fun hehe-haha time and another kirill (hell, i’d even take adrian from deception at this point because at least he meant business and there was an actual bite behind that bark), so i’ll keep wading through the trenches. this one though? into the junk pile, i fear.

will i finish the trilogy? maybe. i’m nosy as hell and i did cackle out loud on several occasions because this was pure comedy in parts, so there’s that. oooooef 🤣💀

i could spend more valuable time whacking this book to death and pointing out all manner of things that rankled me in one of my long(er) rants — bulletpoints and all — because there’s a lot more that i could say but i’m going to clamp my lips here and now. i need to learn to walk away with a one liner sometimes, but i’m a yapper 🥹.

somehow i finished it, so i’ll rate it and call it a day. if you like this, i love it (that) for you 🫶🏾. for me? garbaggioooo (thanks bee). add it to the oxford dictionary.

p.s. cole seems like the only non-insufferable (sufferable?) person in this crew, so does his book hit? asking for a friend 👀 (but if his fmc is that nasty silver, ion know about all that 😩)

You guys, what did I just read?

This was terrible. Okay so this is a contemporary high school bully romance which some people are into, and I'm not judging. I'm somewhat of an enemies to lovers connoisseur myself. Although bully romances aren't my first choice, depending on my mood I could be interested. But this was just... awful lol

So first, the writing is terrible. Seriously, I've read many a fanfictions that are written miles better than this. My god. The same points are repeated over and over. The author forces awkward descriptions into the text in a 4th grade attempt to add "context" and "detail." This may take the crown for worst writing in a book that I've read.

Okay, but fine, maybe I can get past some less than stellar writing if the plot is good. So Elsa starts her high school career at Royal Elite (lol) in England and on her very first day she's minding her own business when Aiden King (lol) comes out of nowhere, LITERALLY grabs her by the neck and shoves her against the wall with his whole soccer team just laughing on, and tells her he will destroy her. I mean, in what world?! She literally just walked into school!

I haven't read many bully romances, but the ones I have are just so unrealistic. And I'm someone who loves wacky fantasy and paranormal tropes, but at least the people in these outlandish scenarios act with some sense. It was just so over the top and unbelievable. Bullies aren't usually so OTT. They do little humiliating things to break people down. They pull mean pranks. They are cruel with words. They don't strangle you and shove you against a wall upon meeting you. That's just a psychopath. And everyone at the school just acts like this is a normal Tuesday. There's a difference between being a bully and being a violent psychopath. Neither is good, but there is a difference and I feel a lot of these books ignore that difference. If you're going to write about a violent psychopath, then fine, but don't play it off like they're just a school bully because- no. Aiden is not a bully. He's insane.

And I likepsychotic characters but the context around them needs to make some sense but it's just 0-100 and I can't suspend my disbelief.

Aiden literally threatens to assault Elsa because she calls him 'Aiden' and not 'King.' This is so extra I can't.

And then! He's sexually assaulting her (literally like 20 min into the book) and she's just sitting there twiddling her thumbs like la dee dah and I'm just like ???????? She's not physically fighting back at all and is just like 'oh Aiden, what do you want now dammit?' 'stop being such a meanie!"

But wait, there's more! After one of Aiden's and Elsa's 'confrontations' (consisting of Aiden threatening to sexually assault her and then doing so) Elsa goes home and is just like, "Ughh. He sucks. But there's something in his eyes?" and then throw a little bit of betraying body in there. Thanks, I hate it.

At least it was sort of entertaining with how bad it was but wow I'm going to go put bleach in my eyes brb

3.5 stars

“Aiden…”
“Hmm, sweetheart?”


Deviant King is your typical bully romance with a mystery and suspense plot and a morally grey hero who wants to destroy the female main character. It’s cliché and cringe but also addicting and entertaining.

This book was much better than Cruel King. I had some expectations based on what I’d heard about this book, the tropes, and the fact that I was drawn to Aiden from the very first book in this series. There was something about his mysterious and quiet personality, but it turns out he’s a sociopath with no morals. Cruel King lacked the depth and intrigue that Deviant King had, and I felt more invested in Aiden and Elsa’s story.

The plot is compelling, with a complex layer of suspense, darkness, mystery, and angst. Aiden and Elsa’s mysterious past plays a major role in this book, hooking you from the very first page. I am not a big fan of bully romance, but Deviant King was different from others in the genre. Aiden and Elsa are bound by their tragic past, the animosity, and the feud between their families, and you can’t help but want to know what happened to them that led them down this path of hate and destruction. It’s not just about bullying—there’s a deep seated history between them that makes their relationship even more intense.

Elsa Quinn is portrayed as a strong, protective, and defiant female character who never shows her weakness or vulnerability in front of anyone. She doesn’t remember her past and was bullied at RES because Aiden made a promise to destroy her. At first, Elsa was just the ice queen who didn’t give a shit about anything or anyone, but it was more about her staying away from unwanted attention while also trying to fit into her new life at RES. However, as the story progressed, we got to see the layers of her character—her strength, her fears, and the way she slowly starts to piece together her past. She never backs down from a challenge, and when Aiden pushes her, she gives as good as she gets. I liked that she’s not a doormat because I really hate it when female characters make their sad life their whole personality.

“Aren’t all girls supposed to be attracted to the white knight? Prince charming? Why the hell am I gravitating towards the villain?”


Aiden King is your typical morally grey character—also a sociopath with no emotions, a deviant with no moral compass, and an anti-hero with a manipulative and possessive obsession. He hides all this behind the façade of the perfect boy at RES. Aiden wants Elsa, so he will do anything to get her where he wants her. He pushes Elsa to her limits, playing mind games until she bows to his command. In short, he is unhinged. I am intrigued by him, but I don’t like him because of what he did to Elsa in this book. I’m hoping to see some redeeming qualities in him in the next books.

“I was never supposed to like you this much. Hell. I wasn’t supposed to think about you more than I think of myself.”


Aiden and Elsa have crazy and explosive chemistry. There’s animosity and hate between them, but they also have a few sweet and endearing moments in this book. One minute, Aiden is forcing Elsa to do what he commands, and the next, he’s calling her adorable and sweetheart. He’s unhinged, but at least he owns it. I couldn’t help but root for him in this book. What started as hate and destruction slowly evolved into attraction, lust, tension, and maybe even love. I hated how he bullied her, but I also liked how Elsa fought back. The way she gets on his nerves every time was so funny, and I love it when Aiden is pissed and jealous. They are a match made in hell.

“There’s nothing I wouldn’t do to have you, sweetheart.”
“Nothing?”
“Absolutely nothing.”


I still hated that the main characters were teenagers, and I had to brainwash myself into believing they were in their early 20s, but at least Aiden and Elsa did not have 2D personalities like Levi and Astrid. The writing still needs a lot of work. It’s cringy, and the dialogue had me laughing most of the time because of how these teenagers behaved like they were the kings of the world. But despite the flaws, the story kept me engaged.

So far, the story is good, and the plot moves at a solid pace. There are no major revelations in this book, and I’m hoping to learn more about Aiden and Elsa’s past in the next instalments. There are so many truths to be revealed, mysteries to unfold, and pasts to unravel—and I’m so here for it.

This book in a couple of gif's:





So, this was my first ever bully romance and I loved it so much. (In case you're wondering, I read this book about 3 months ago, and I've come a long way since then in this trope. The reason I'm writing this review now is because when I read this book I hadn't starting writing reviews yet, and I just re-read this series so I thought why not write one now?) Anyways, like I said this was my first book in this trope and my first book by author Rina Kent, who btw is now one of my fav authors💖

Review

I loved this book so much!!

“They say it doesn’t take long for your life to be flipped upside down. A moment. A second. And it’s all over. I should’ve known. If I had, I would’ve done things differently. Maybe I would’ve walked the other way. Maybe my tale wouldn’t have ended the way it did. But the thing about ‘maybes’? They’re useless.”

Elsa Quinn, comes to Royal Elite, in hopes of doing well and getting into Cambridge which is her dream college but all goes to hell when Aiden King publicly declares war against her by saying "I will destroy you"

“Be mine and you become the queen on my board.” He pauses and flicks his tongue to lick my lower lip. “Fight and you’ll remain a pawn.”

Aiden King is the most popular guy on campus. He is dark and broody and doesn't talk much. The four of them (Ronan Astor, Cole Nash, Xander Knight and 'the mighty king' himself) are also known as the 'Four Horseman.' They are the golden boys of the town and loved by all.

Everyone knows the mighty Aiden who isn't affected by much, but when Elsa joins RES, he is affected by her presence like an itch to scratch.


(Totally inappropriate, I know, but I just couldn't resist it😂)

So anyways, no one knows why he is so affected by her presence, buuuut we find out his reasons as the story progresses and let me tell you..


I loved Elsa so much, she WASN'T a doormat at all and stood her own. Oh, and her friendship with Kim...*I'm not swooning over the friendship more than the relationship*
Honestly, she was like a momma bear, protecting Kim from all the fat-shaming and bullying. She was so strong and resilient and even though she was getting bullied too, she tried her best to protect Kim.


What an ending!! The cliff-hanger was ahh-maz-ing!!

Me at the end of the book:





I so enjoyed this book, and if you're looking for a good, dark, captivating bully romance, this book is highly recommended!!

This book may contain some dubious content as it's a dark, bully romance. But if you're okay with it I would highly recommend this book!

3.5 stars ִ ࣪𖤐.ᐟ

The ENDING?! HELP-

“Those who don’t play think that the king is the most important piece because the game is over when he dies. They don’t know that the king is useless without his queen.”


This was so trash but I couldn’t look away?

Aiden is… I’m not even quite sure how to describe him. He’s a manipulative psychopath who takes ‘obsessive and possessive’ pretty seriously, and has a personal vendetta against the word ‘no’ (CHECK TRIGGERS BEFORE READING). I had a love/hate relationship with him - sometimes he’d do or say something protective that I’d find almost charming (I was going to say ‘sweet’ but that could not be more wrong, even ‘charming’ is pushing it..), but other times I wanted to wring his bloody neck in. Correction: most times.

Elsa ran into hard walls that turned out to be hard chests so many times that I’m surprised she didn’t get a concussion. I also wish she’d just punch Aiden in the face at least once☝🏻. However, when she properly stood up to Silver, I stood up myself and applauded💃🏼, and I’m interested to see how her past will unfold (let’s just ignore the fact some of it has already been spoiled for me🤧).

The writing is.. well it’s there. It kind of just does the job. I just cannot shake the feeling that this is a non-British person’s attempt at writing British characters, even though Rina Kent IS British😭. It’s atrocious. The way “wanker” and “arsehole” are thrown in randomly makes me cringe lmao. They’re not the only two words in our vocabulary Rina, you should know this😔.

Overall though, whilst Elsa and Aiden’s romance developed a bit too quickly for my liking, I had been craving a trashy romance (sometimes they’re just what a girl needs lol) and this delivered. It was entertaining🤷‍♀️.

“Besides, did you miss the part where I’m mad at you?”
“I’m mad at you, too. We can be mad at each other while you’re sitting on my lap.”

If you’re trying to make your character dark and menacing at least try to make them appear, I don’t know, convincing??
A boy who throttles an unsuspecting girl he DOESN’T know after he JUST makes eye contact with her is anything but menacing. He doesn’t belong in a school that only accepts one percent of the iNteLliGent students (umm, this school needs to conduct a serious reevaluation). He belongs in a mental asylum.

“His other hand clutches my jaw, and my lips tremble at the thought that he’ll snap my neck.
“W-What are you doing?”
He leans forward so his mouth hovers inches away from mine and growls. “I will destroy you.”
Those words seal my fate.”

The hero’s first meeting with the heroine, everyone. Can you imagine the derisive laugh I had to STIFLE after reading that?! 😃😃

I did not expect such behavior from someone named AIDEN KING!?!?

Disappointing 😍

4/5 ⭐️ This was my first book by Rina Kent and it is what made me fall in love with her books. It is definitely not perfect but it will always hold a special place in my heart. It was also the first bully romance I ever read.

It just felt so comforting to be back in the Royal Elite world. And I just melted each time Aiden’s psycho self called Elsa sweetheart 🫠🫠

And he could be so sweet too 🥹 I loved it when he got the school to serve Elsa’s special food. She could never eat the cafeteria food before because of her heart condition. So he made it happen for her 🥹. And I also loved how he always brought her water after practice. And his jealousy over anyone being near his Elsa? It was so much fun 😭🫠🥹. It literally had me giggling 🤭

I did rate this 5 stars the first time I read it but I just didn’t get the 5 stars feel like last time. I still loved it though! 🥰 Aiden King will always be my favorite 😌
